content: Kaohsiung Medical University, previously known as Kaohsiung Medical College, is a private university located in Kaohsiung, Taiwan. It is widely regarded as the premier institution for medical research and education in the Kaohsiung region. The university was established in 1954 by Frank C. Chen, a former mayor of Kaohsiung, who donated land for the college, and Professor Tu Tsung-ming, Taiwan's first Doctor of Medicine. Upon its founding, it became the first private medical institution in Southern Taiwan. Professor Tu, the first president of the college, emphasized a philosophy centered on the joy of learning, prioritizing research, striving for progress, and contributing to global well-being. In August 1999, the institution transitioned from Kaohsiung Medical College to Kaohsiung Medical University with approval from Taiwan's Ministry of Education. This change was made to address the increasing internationalization of society and to meet emerging challenges. The university has consistently received superior ratings in all categories under the Ministry of Education's Mid-term School Administration Development Plan. Three years after its establishment, the university founded its hospital in June 1957, now known as Chung-Ho Memorial Hospital, Kaohsiung Medical University. This hospital has grown to become the largest medical center in Southern Taiwan. It serves a threefold mission of education, research, and healthcare service, training students and faculty while safeguarding the health of the region. In 1998, the university entered into an agreement with the Kaohsiung Municipal Government to manage Hsiao-kang Hospital, which continues to provide medical care and community health services. Teaching Kaohsiung Medical University maintains a teacher-to-student ratio of 1:12, surpassing the standards set by Taiwan's Ministry of Education. With financial support from private funding and government subsidies, the university is able to implement diverse employment programs to attract distinguished scholars and educators from both Taiwan and abroad. The university offers up to 35 million New Taiwan dollars in scholarships and student grants annually. Research Kaohsiung Medical University is recognized as a leading medical research institution in Southern Taiwan, with a strong team of highly qualified and experienced researchers. The university operates four university-level research centers, six specialized research centers, and 20 interdisciplinary research teams, all of which include experts from various fields. The institution actively promotes interdisciplinary research and fosters collaboration between teams working on basic science and clinical applications. The MedicoGenomic Research Center at the university has developed a diagnostic chip for colorectal cancer and identified molecular markers (both DNA and RNA) for tumors, which are applicable in both laboratory and clinical settings. The Functional Proteomics Research Center conducts systematic studies on cellular proteins, including their types, functions, expression patterns, and post-translational modifications. The Chinese Herbal Medicine and New Drug Research Center focuses on creating new drug models based on herbal medicines and developing herbal prescriptions that meet international standards.
